_provenance.note: Maine citation authorities. Maine's operative SNAP policy manual is 10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 301 (Code of Maine Rules), cited by a hyphenated section-number convention such as '111-7' (ABAWD), '999-2' (Geographic Exemptions), '999-3' (Appendix Charts). This pack also cites Maine Revised Statutes, 22 M.R.S. § 3104 and its subsections, for the drug-felony opt-out, violent-crime disqualification, and categorical-eligibility statutory basis, so this pack defines a SECOND citation family, 'memrs', matching this roster's Nebraska, Connecticut, Kentucky, Alabama, and Louisiana packs' multi-family pattern.

patterns.note: Maine DHHS SNAP Rules, 10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 301, cited by bare hyphenated section number, e.g. 111-7 (Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents), 999-2 (Geographic Exemptions from ABAWD Work Requirements), 999-3 (Appendix Charts).

Maine Revised Statutes, Title 22 (Health and Welfare), § 3104 (Statewide Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and § 3104-A. This pack cites subsections (13) categorical eligibility, (14) drug-conviction opt-out, and (15) violent-crime/sexual-assault felon ineligibility.

mecmr.note: Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) — work-registration and time-limit criteria, amended by SNAP Rule #240A/#240P for OBBBA compliance (age range 18-64, caregiver exemption narrowed to child under 14)
Household composition and "separate household" determinations, including subsection (2)(c) referenced by the 165% FPL income test for elderly/disabled individuals living with others
Geographic Exemptions from ABAWD Work Requirements — lists Maine's waived areas when an active waiver exists; amended by SNAP Rule #234A (213 areas, FY2025, expired 9/30/2025)

Appendix — Charts 1 through 9: 100%/130%/165%/200% FPL income tables, maximum allotments, minimum benefit, Standard Deduction, shelter/utility allowance chart, asset-limit chart. Updated via periodic numbered SNAP Rules (e.g. Rule #244, FFY2026 Budgeting Figures and FPL Updates)

Referenced in SNAP Rule #241/#242 amendments alongside § 555-5 (2025-12-14 filings) — this pack did not independently verify the substantive content of this section beyond its rulemaking-history listing

Household income-limit exemptions referenced by the Section 999-3 chart notes ("households must have incomes below the appropriate income limits unless exempt per Section 444-8") — this pack did not independently fetch this section's full substantive text

memrs.note: Categorical eligibility — directs the Department to adopt rules maximizing SNAP access for households that would be TANF-dependent-child households but do not receive a cash grant; statutory basis for Maine's 200% FPL Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) pathway

Prohibition against denial of assistance based on drug conviction — Maine's FULL opt-out of the federal drug-felony SNAP ban: an otherwise-eligible person may not be denied SNAP because of a drug-related felony conviction. FLAGSHIP CORRECTION: a February 2026 secondary source (prisonpolicy.org) miscategorized Maine as NOT having opted out.

Separate, narrower ineligibility for individuals convicted on or after 1/1/2018 of aggravated sexual abuse, murder, an 18 U.S.C. Chapter 110 offense, or a VAWA-defined sexual-assault offense (or a substantially similar Maine offense), while not in compliance with sentence/parole/probation terms or as a fleeing felon. Distinct from, and should not be conflated with, the drug-felony provision in subsection (14).

Referenced in SNAP Rule #244's Fact Sheet as additional statutory authority considered for general SNAP eligibility and benefit levels; this pack did not independently fetch this section's full text separately from § 3104
